title: The Recipe of the quarry
premise: Isandro Brightwater, a quiet coder at Quarry Hill Academy, runs an anonymous account that documents the school's small injustices—until the senior college essay prompt, 'Tell us a truth you've never said aloud,' unlocks a flood of confessions, including one that hints at a fatal accident the school board buried in the old quarry a decade ago. When his best friend Priya's audition for the conservatory is threatened by the same board members who covered it up, Isandro must choose between his invisibility and the truth. Digging through archives, corrupted backups, and a janitor's fading memory, he rebuilds the buried record while falling for Marisol, the board chair's daughter, whose loyalty is torn between family and justice. In the final audition, Isandro streams the exposed evidence to the whole school, forcing the board's resignation and winning Priya her rightful place—though the cost is his anonymity, his safety, and a love that must survive being seen at last.
about_author: Marguerite Villalobos is a former debate coach who grew up in a quarry town where the water ran turquoise and the records ran thin. She writes stories about teenagers who refuse to let institutions do their remembering for them.

chapters.title: Head Down, Grades Up
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. We meet his careful, coded life at Quarry Hill Academy: flawless homework, closed locker, and the anonymous account 'quarrylight' that logs small injustices no one reads. Beat: controlled loneliness, the comfort of invisibility.

chapters.title: The Prompt
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. English teacher Mr. Okafor unveils the college essay question—'a truth you've never said aloud'—and the room goes electric. Isandro's draft cursor blinks over a truth he won't type. Beat: dread disguised as routine.

chapters.title: Priya's Audition Piece
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya rehearses cello for the conservatory final audition; her scholarship hinges on the board's last-minute 'facility review.' She jokes about the quarry's bad acoustics; Isandro goes still. Beat: warmth shadowed by foreboding.

chapters.title: Forty Confessions
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Anonymous essay drafts leak onto a shared drive he administers. One mentions 'the year the quarry took someone' and a name: Danny Ferro, class of 2014. Beat: the first crack in his safe world.

chapters.title: Marisol at the Fence
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Marisol Vega, board chair's daughter, catches Isandro photographing the sealed quarry gate. Their banter is sharp, unwilling, alive. Beat: attraction arriving at the worst possible moment.

chapters.title: The Board's Quiet Vote
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya overhears her mother, a board secretary, shredding 'legacy files' before the facility review. The audition venue is suddenly moved—off campus. Beat: betrayal by institution.

chapters.title: Danny Ferro
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Yearbooks, a memorial page quietly deleted, a scholarship renamed. Danny fell into the quarry during a school-sanctioned 'team building' night; the record ends there. Beat: cold clarity of purpose.

chapters.title: The Janitor Who Remembers
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Gus, the night custodian, hums Danny's favorite song and lets slip that he 'saw what he saw' before his memory began to fail. Beat: grief as a living thing.

chapters.title: Locker Shut
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Vice Principal Reyes searches lockers after the leaked essays; Isandro's encryption saves him, but Priya's draft is confiscated. Beat: paranoia tightening like a wire.

chapters.title: Marisol's Inheritance
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. At dinner, Marisol's father praises 'protecting the school's reputation' over dessert. She finds her mother's old yearbook—Danny Ferro's photo circled. Beat: loyalty beginning to splinter.

chapters.title: The Corrupted Backup
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Isandro recovers fragments from a 2014 district server: incident report, then a gap where the conclusion should be, overwritten the same week. Beat: the thrill and terror of proof that proves too little.

chapters.title: First Lie to Marisol
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Marisol asks what he's really doing at the quarry; Isandro lies badly. She lets him. Beat: love against duty, both of them hiding.

chapters.title: Priya's Warning
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya finds Isandro's notes and begs him to stop—her audition is in three weeks, and the board punishes association. Beat: friendship strained between safety and truth.

chapters.title: Gus's Box
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Gus, lucid for one bright hour, hands over a maintenance log: a gate unlocked that night, a supervisor's initials—R. Vega. Beat: the past handing Isandro a live grenade.

chapters.title: The Essay He Won't Write
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Mr. Okafor conferences with Isandro about his blank essay. 'A truth unsaid is still a choice,' he says. Beat: guilt sharpened into a question.

chapters.title: Marisol Reads the Log
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Isandro shows Marisol the maintenance log. She recognizes her father's handwriting and, worse, doesn't doubt it. Beat: heartbreak as evidence.

chapters.title: The Account Breached
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. 'quarrylight' is traced partway; Reyes suspends a wrong student, Theo, in Isandro's place. Beat: the cost of anonymity paid by the innocent.

chapters.title: Confession by Proxy
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Isandro turns himself in obliquely—submitting his college essay, the truth at last: Danny Ferro, the quarry, the cover-up. Beat: relief and exposure braided together.

chapters.title: Suspended
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Isandro is suspended pending 'investigation'; the essay is sealed as 'evidence.' Priya realizes the board will bury him like they buried Danny. Beat: rage crystallizing into alliance.

chapters.title: The Archive Room
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Marisol uses her father's keycard at midnight, copying board minutes from 2014: an emergency session, a settlement, a gag order. Beat: treason as an act of love.

chapters.title: What Gus Forgot
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Gus's memory fails mid-interview; he can't recall the crucial night, only the song. Isandro realizes memory needs a vessel—records, witnesses, art. Beat: tenderness and urgency.

chapters.title: Priya's Decision
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya chooses to premiere her audition piece as a composition built from Danny Ferro's recovered voicemails and the quarry's echo. Beat: art as testimony.

chapters.title: Threats, Politely Worded
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. A lawyer's letter arrives at Isandro's home; his parents, frightened, demand he stop. Beat: the family cost of justice outside the law.

chapters.title: Marisol Confronts Her Father
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Marisol asks her father directly about Danny. He doesn't deny it; he explains it. That's worse. Beat: the death of a childhood certainty.

chapters.title: The Backup of the Backup
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Isandro reconstructs the overwritten report from print spool caches and an old teacher's email archive: negligence, then deliberate concealment, signed by four sitting board members. Beat: triumph shadowed by fear of what comes next.

chapters.title: Allies in Detention
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Theo, exonerated, joins the cause; students begin leaving anonymous truths in Danny's old locker like offerings. Beat: a movement quietly assembling.

chapters.title: The Gag Order
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. The district threatens legal action against anyone publishing 'sealed records.' Isandro encrypts everything and distributes keys. Beat: defiance with a deadline.

chapters.title: Marisol's Choice
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Marisol must decide whether to testify. She records her own college essay—the truth about her father—as both confession and commitment. Beat: love against duty, resolved toward duty.

chapters.title: The Leak That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. A decoy leak flushes out who's watching 'quarrylight': it's Reyes, acting for the board chair. Beat: the trap inverted.

chapters.title: Two Days Before the Audition
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Final rehearsal; her hands shake. Isandro promises the truth will be in the room with her. Beat: terror transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: The Night Before
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Isandro and Marisol stage the evidence on the school's own servers, timestamped to release during the livestreamed audition. Gus, in the audience, is their witness. Beat: hushed, held breath.

chapters.title: The Final Audition
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya plays the Ferro piece; mid-performance, the archive unlocks on every screen in the auditorium. Beat: the climax's first detonation—art and evidence in one breath.

chapters.title: What the Screens Said
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. The 2014 minutes, the settlement, the signatures—Vega's name in the board's own hand. Chaos, then a silence in which no one can un-see it. Beat: catharsis.

chapters.title: Vega's Fall
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Marisol stands and reads her essay aloud, publicly severing herself from the cover-up. Her father resigns before the last page. Beat: devastating, liberating grief.

chapters.title: The Board's Resignations
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Three more resignations; the state opens an inquiry; Danny Ferro's name returns to the scholarship. Isandro's suspension is rescinded—by the students who demanded it. Beat: justice arriving, imperfect and real.

chapters.title: Priya's Standing Ovation
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The conservatory panel, unmoved by scandal, offers Priya admission on merit—and she accepts on her own terms. Beat: joy earned twice over.

chapters.title: Gus Remembers Enough
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. At the quarry's edge, Gus tells the whole story to the gathered students, memory held together by their listening. Beat: memory as a communal act.

chapters.title: Marisol at the Fence, Again
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Isandro and Marisol meet where they first argued. No lies left between them; something new begins, unhidden. Beat: love surviving the light.

chapters.title: The Essay, Submitted
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Isandro mails his true college essay—signed, unanonymous. Mr. Okafor reads it and says only, 'Finally.' Beat: quiet completion.

chapters.title: The Recipe of the Quarry
chapters.summary: Ensemble coda. One year later: the quarry is a memorial garden, the account 'quarrylight' now belongs to every student who posts a truth. Isandro, Priya, and Marisol add Danny's name to the stone. Beat: memory kept, justice ongoing, love unhidden.
